_comment: Procurement-policy layer of the Procurement Knowledge Graph (General Financial Rules 2017 and public-procurement orders). Each policy node carries its source and verification state. Clause templates are inserted by the Tender Synthesizer; 'advisory' policies are shown to the officer but not written into the tender. Monetary thresholds change — verify on doe.gov.in / dpiit.gov.in before use.

policies.title: GFR 2017 Rule 144 — Fundamental principles of public buying
policies.summary: Specifications must meet the essential needs, be objective, functional, generic and measurable, and must not favour a brand; procurement must be efficient, economical and transparent.

clause.heading: Brand Neutrality
clause.text: No brand or make is specified; any product that meets these specifications and the cited Indian Standards is acceptable.

policies.title: GFR 2017 Rule 149 — Procurement through GeM
policies.summary: Common-use goods available on GeM are procured through GeM: up to Rs 50,000 directly; Rs 50,000–10 lakh from the lowest-priced of at least three OEMs/sellers; above Rs 10 lakh through GeM bidding / reverse auction.

policies.title: GFR 2017 Rule 161 — Advertised tender enquiry
policies.summary: Advertised tender enquiry for estimated value of Rs 50 lakh and above; minimum three weeks for domestic bid submission (four weeks for global).

policies.title: GFR 2017 Rule 170 — Bid security
policies.summary: Bid security ordinarily 2–5% of the estimated value; may be replaced by a Bid Securing Declaration where permitted; MSEs registered with the notified bodies are exempt.

clause.heading: Bid Security (EMD)
clause.text: Bid security of Rs. {emd} (2% of the estimated value) shall be furnished with the bid; Micro and Small Enterprises registered as per the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs are exempted on submission of a valid registration certificate.

policies.title: GFR 2017 Rule 171 — Performance security
policies.summary: Performance security of a percentage of the contract value (range as notified by the Department of Expenditure), valid for 60 days beyond completion of all contractual obligations including warranty.

clause.heading: Performance Security
clause.text: The successful bidder shall furnish a performance security of 5% of the contract value within 14 days of the award, valid for 60 days beyond the completion of all contractual obligations including the warranty period.

policies.title: Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, 2017 (revised 16-09-2020)
policies.summary: Class-I local suppliers (local content of at least 50%) get purchase preference; Class-II (at least 20%) may participate; the nodal ministry may notify higher local content.

clause.heading: Make in India
clause.text: Purchase preference shall be given to Class-I local suppliers as per the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, 2017 as amended; bidders shall declare the percentage of local content and the location of value addition.

policies.title: Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) Order, 2012 (amended)
policies.summary: MSEs get free tender documents, exemption from bid security and purchase preference; ministries have an annual MSE procurement target.

clause.heading: Micro and Small Enterprises
clause.text: Benefits to Micro and Small Enterprises shall be extended as per the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs Order, 2012 as amended, on submission of valid Udyam registration.
